name: Henadad
overview: Henadad was a male official responsible for the other half of the district of Keilah, as noted in Nehemiah 3:18. His role signifies a position of local authority during the period of Jerusalem's restoration. No additional tribal or personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Henadad means 'favor of Hadad,' reflecting a proper name of Semitic origin. This meaning highlights a cultural connection but is not indicated as a divine name given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Henadad as the father of Bavvai, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Henadad's significance lies in his official capacity during the rebuilding efforts of Jerusalem, specifically overseeing part of Keilah. His mention underscores the organized and communal nature of the restoration work under Nehemiah's leadership. Though a minor figure, Henadad contributes to the broader narrative of God's providential care in restoring His people and city.
